text:
elaine-support: quick heads-up — customer Tyler reports invoice INV-2026-03-47 has a higher reserved GPU hour line than what their dashboard shows for pool rdp-42. invoice: 1,320h, dashboard reserved_hours: 1,200h, dashboard burst_hours: 80h. they say token burn looks normal and they didn't trigger extra load. can someone triage?

tyler-customer: adding context from our side — usage graphs (region eu-west1) show fairly steady throughput. We ran a report across Feb and saw ~4.6B tokens, latency normal. Expectation was roughly 1.2k reserved hours billed. Invoice surprised us.

marta-finance: noted. invoice line is under "Dedicated - rdp-42 - Feb". I can share invoice PDF. Concern: we budgeted 1.2k reserved hours. If 1.32k billed that’s ~10% over. Customer is asking for an explanation or credit.

elaine-support: TY. tagging @raj-eng to pull metering logs and reconciliation. Also @ops-bot — can you post any automated metering alerts from that window?

ops-bot: scheduled job metering-recon ran 2026-02-01..2026-02-28: status=complete, anomalies=2 (both <0.5% variance). Log ID: met-recon-20260228-7c9

raj-eng: I can start with two quick checks: 1) were burst_hours double-counted into reserved line; 2) billing window vs dashboard timezone alignment. Sharing my first query.

raj-eng: ```
-- rough aggregation from metering DB
SELECT pool_id, SUM(reserved_gpu_hours) AS reserved_hours, SUM(burst_gpu_hours) AS burst_hours
FROM metering.usage
WHERE pool_id = 'rdp-42' AND usage_date BETWEEN '2026-02-01' AND '2026-02-28'
GROUP BY pool_id;
```

raj-eng: result (local dev run): reserved_hours=1200.00, burst_hours=120.00, total=1320.00. this matches invoice (1,320) but dashboard reserved_hours shows 1,200 and burst_hours shows 80. so invoice total = reserved + burst; dashboard seems to be showing reserved_hours and under-reporting burst by 40h.

elaine-support: interesting — customer dashboard displays burst separately in the UI but their exported CSV shows only 80h for burst. Is there a lag?

raj-eng: possible causes: 1) late attribution (some burst events were recorded after the dashboard CSV snapshot), 2) different aggregation windows (billing uses UTC day boundaries, dashboard uses tenant timezone), 3) a de-dupe bug in dashboard rendering that collapsed some short burst events.

marta-finance: invoice uses UTC billing period. If dashboard is local tz then sums can differ if there are events near month edges. Customer insists they didn't run anything at the end of the month but they did have a Canary rollout on Feb 28 23:58 UTC.

tyler-customer: correct — we did a small canary at 23:58 UTC to 00:06 UTC (short ramp). The canary hit burst routing to the dedicated pool. We thought it would be charged as burst (expected ~8m) — but didn't expect 40 extra hours.

raj-eng: that short window could generate many short autoscale events depending on min-granularity. If our metering counts each preemption or scale step as a full slot-minute, aggregation bugs could inflate burst hours. I'll pull raw event stream for Feb 28 23:50..00:10 UTC.

raj-eng: ```
# sample API to fetch events
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $METER_TOKEN" "https://metering.internal/api/v1/events?pool=rdp-42&start=2026-02-28T23:50:00Z&end=2026-03-01T00:10:00Z" | jq '.'
```

raj-eng: initial scan shows many rapid scale-in/scale-out entries (~480 events) each with partial durations ~5-15s. Our slot-hour rounding code currently rounds up to nearest minute per event before summing minutes -> hours. If UI pipeline does a different rollup (aggregate durations first then round) that explains discrepancy.

elaine-support: can you quantify the delta if we instead aggregate durations first?

raj-eng: did a delta calc: event-round-up method -> 40.0h extra; aggregate-first then round -> 0.67h. So rounding strategy explains almost all of the 40h.

marta-finance: that matches customer delta (invoice - dashboard burst = 40h). What's our policy? Billing currently charges based on raw metering pipeline (per-event rounding), and UI CSV uses aggregate-first. That mismatch is bad.

elaine-support: customer-facing ask: either refund/credit the 40h or update invoice explanation. Tyler prefers credit but is open to a clarified bill if it's our policy.

marta-finance: recommend we offer provisional credit while we fix mismatch and then reconcile. I'll draft a credit note for ~40h * pool rate and hold for ops sign-off.

raj-eng: engineering action items: A1) patch metering aggregation to use aggregate-first rounding for burst events; A2) backfill corrected burst hours for Feb for affected pools (rdp-42); A3) add unit test to prevent reintroducing per-event rounding. I can PR A1 today.

elaine-support: ty. @tyler-customer I'll loop you back with credit note and ETA for reconciliation. Estimated fix+backfill timeline: 48h after PR merge.

tyler-customer: appreciate the quick triage. Please keep billing as provisional until resolved.

ops-bot: ticket created: MTR-1279 "burst metering rounding mismatch" assigned -> raj-eng.

marta-finance: I'll prepare provisional credit and attach to INV-2026-03-47 pending final backfill.

elaine-support: closing loop for now. Next steps: raj -> PR + backfill plan; marta -> provisional credit; i'll update customer and close once backfill done. Thanks all.
